title: Registro Formale e Informale nella Scrittura
subtitle: Choosing vocabulary and structure to match the situation.
objectives: Identify markers of formal vs. informal written register
Rewrite an informal sentence in a formal register and vice versa
Use standard formal opening/closing formulas for emails and letters

content.intro: Beyond tu vs. Lei, Italian marks formality through vocabulary choice, sentence structure, and set phrases — especially visible in written communication.
content.explanation: Formal writing favors longer, more explicit sentences, the connectors from the previous lesson, and a vocabulary that avoids colloquialisms. Informal writing (texts, casual emails to friends) allows contractions, colloquial vocabulary, and much shorter sentences.

rules.heading: a) Vocabulary pairs (informal → formal)
rules.body: un sacco di → molti/numerosi; un po' → un po' (fine) / leggermente; fare un giro → effettuare una visita; iniziare → dare inizio a; dire → comunicare, dichiarare

rules.heading: b) Email/letter formulas
rules.body:
• Formal opening: Gentile Sig.ra/Sig. [Cognome], La contatto per...
  • Formal closing: Cordiali saluti / Distinti saluti
  • Informal opening: Ciao [Nome],
  • Informal closing: A presto! / Un abbraccio

examples.it: Gentile Dott.ssa Rossi, Le scrivo per chiederLe informazioni riguardo al Suo prossimo seminario.
examples.en: Dear Dr. Rossi, I am writing to ask you for information about your upcoming seminar.

examples.it: Ciao Marco, ti scrivo per chiederti se sei libero sabato!
examples.en: Hi Marco, I'm writing to ask if you're free Saturday!

examples.it: La informiamo che la Sua richiesta è stata accolta.
examples.en: We inform you that your request has been accepted.

examples.it: Ti volevo dire che ho accettato il lavoro!
examples.en: I wanted to tell you I accepted the job!

commonMistakes.wrong: Ciao Direttore, volevo sapere... (mixing informal greeting with a formal context)
commonMistakes.why: Mixing an informal opening with formal content and pronouns is inconsistent — pick one register and keep it throughout.

commonMistakes.wrong: Ending a formal email with Ciao!
commonMistakes.right: Ending with Cordiali saluti / Distinti saluti
commonMistakes.why: Ciao is strictly informal — a formal closing formula is expected to match a Lei-register email.

items.prompt: Which closing fits a formal email to a company?
items.explanation: Cordiali saluti is the standard formal closing.

items.prompt: Which is the more formal way to say "a lot of people"?
items.explanation: Numerose persone is the formal-register equivalent.

items.incorrect: Gentile Direttore, ciao! Volevo un po' di info.
answer: Gentile Direttore, Le scrivo per richiedere alcune informazioni.
items.explanation: A formal opening (Gentile Direttore) should be followed by consistently formal vocabulary and structure, not casual expressions.
Gentile is the standard formal opening.

items.prompt: Un ___ di persone ha partecipato all'evento. (informal "a lot of")
items.explanation: Un sacco di is a colloquial, informal expression.

items.prompt: La ringrazio e Le porgo i miei ___ saluti. (formal closing word)
items.explanation: Distinti/cordiali saluti are standard formal closings.
Ciao is the standard informal opening.

items.prompt: La informiamo che la Sua richiesta ___ (essere) stata accolta.
items.explanation: Formal passive, third person singular.

items.prompt: Ti volevo ___ (dire) che ho accettato il lavoro! (informal)
items.explanation: Dire is the plain, informal verb; comunicare/dichiarare are the formal equivalents.

items.prompt: ___ ringraziarLa per la disponibilità. (formal, "I would like to")
items.explanation: Vorrei is the polite, formal way to open a request.
Un abbraccio is a warm, informal closing.

items.prompt: Which is the formal equivalent of "iniziare"?
items.explanation: Dare inizio a is the more formal, written equivalent.

items.prompt: Which opening fits a formal letter to someone whose name you don't know?
items.explanation: Egregio Signore is a standard formal opening.

items.prompt: Which is more informal: "un po'" or "leggermente"?
items.explanation: Un po' is the everyday, informal choice; leggermente is more formal.

items.prompt: Which verb is the formal equivalent of "dire"?
items.explanation: Comunicare/dichiarare are the formal equivalents of dire.

items.prompt: What marks informal written Italian, besides vocabulary?
items.explanation: Informal writing favors contractions and shorter sentences.

items.prompt: Which closing would be inconsistent in a formal email?
items.explanation: Ciao ciao is strictly informal, inconsistent with a formal email.

items.prompt: "Effettuare una visita" is the formal equivalent of...
items.explanation: Effettuare una visita is the formal register version of fare un giro.

items.prompt: What should you do if you start an email formally?
options: keep the whole email formal, consistently
mix in informal phrases for warmth
switch to informal for the closing
items.explanation: Consistency of register matters more than any single word.
Formal writing favors precise, non-colloquial vocabulary.

items.statement: Tu and Lei are the only markers of formality in Italian.
items.explanation: Vocabulary, sentence structure, and set phrases also mark formality.

items.statement: Cordiali saluti is an appropriate closing for a casual text to a friend.
items.explanation: It's a formal closing, inconsistent with a casual text.

items.statement: Contractions and colloquial vocabulary are typical of informal writing.
items.explanation: These are hallmarks of informal register.

items.statement: Mixing a formal opening with informal vocabulary throughout is considered good style.
items.explanation: Consistency of register matters — mixing them is inconsistent.

items.statement: "Numerose persone" is more formal than "un sacco di gente".
items.explanation: Numerose persone is the formal-register equivalent.

items.statement: Formal writing tends to use shorter, more fragmented sentences than informal writing.
items.explanation: Formal writing tends toward longer, more explicit sentences.

items.statement: Set opening/closing formulas exist for both formal and informal correspondence.
items.explanation: Both registers have their own standard formulas.

summary: Formal register favors explicit, longer sentences and formal vocabulary; informal favors contractions and colloquialisms.
Set formulas exist for opening/closing formal and informal correspondence — don't mix them.
Consistency matters more than any single word choice: pick a register and hold it throughout.
